draft_text: On the Brindle-Voice test set, Brisling may decode faster than Talmar (median latency 41 vs 118 ms per utterance).
revised_text: On the Brindle-Voice test set, Brisling may decode faster than Talmar (median latency 41 vs 118 ms per utterance).
rationale: Latency values match (41 vs 118 ms). However, the claim uses "may decode faster," which is appropriately hedged. But note the latencies were measured on different hardware (Brisling on Corvex A2 fp16; Talmar on Corvex A1 fp32), so the comparison is not apples-to-apples. The hedge "may" is appropriate given no statistical test and differing measurement conditions. The claim is supported as stated with appropriate hedging.

data.notes: Talmar latency is the value reported by Ruiz-Hale et al. (2023) on Corvex A1 (fp32, batch size 1); all other latencies were measured by us on Corvex A2 (fp16, batch size 1).

observations.message: No statistical test is reported for this comparison. This means statistical significance is NOT established; it is NOT evidence that the effect is absent or that the methods are equivalent.
